title: Pathfinder: per-route cohort lineage, drift scorer, and automated recovery actions
creator: Lina Torres
description:
Problem: Engineers currently lack a single, explainable surface in Console that ties per-route traces, cohort lineage, and a quantitative drift score together to power safe canary/A-B rollouts and automated recovery decisions. Without this, teams either overreact to noisy signals or wait too long to revert, causing customer impact and higher token cost.

Goal: Deliver 'Pathfinder' — a Console feature combining (1) cohort lineage viz (traffic split -> sampling -> downstream traces), (2) a lightweight drift scorer (multi-metric) that outputs a human-readable signal and confidence band, and (3) an actionable recovery builder (auto-restore / staged rollback templates) that can execute safe, auditable recovery steps.

Scope: Console UI components (dashboards + trace-link), server-side telemetry pipeline for drift scoring, rollout policy DSL integration, and a minimal API hook to trigger automated recovery actions. This scope excludes building new model-side instrumentation and excludes deep ML-based root cause analysis (we will integrate in a follow-up).
objectives: Expose per-route cohort lineage in Console for canary/A-B/shadow traffic
Compute and surface a deterministic drift score combining latency, error-rate, token-utilization, and semantic divergence (embedding cosine)
Provide pre-flight safety checks and an automated recovery action builder (canary shrink, reroute, or full revert) with audit logging
Link cohort rows to related traces and example requests for fast triage
acceptance_criteria: Console shows cohort lineage for any rollout with >1 variant and captures request sampling links
Drift score is computed every minute and available in per-route charts and as a cohort metric via API
Automated recovery actions can be created in the UI, require a two-step confirmation, and generate an audit log entry with exec trace
End-to-end test that creates a synthetic drift (in test env) and triggers the recommended action with proper rollback
Performance: drift scoring pipeline adds <150ms p95 processing overhead to telemetry ingestion and is horizontally scalable
telemetry_metrics: trace_link_rate (percent of cohort requests with attached trace)
rollout_plan: MVP week 1: Gather schema requirements, sample data, and build mockups (UI + API contract)
MVP week 2: Implement drift scorer prototype in telemetry pipeline + unit tests
MVP week 3: Console dashboard and trace-link integration + internal dogfood rollout
MVP week 4: Recovery action builder and audit log; integration test and e2e smoke
Canary: gated behind feature flag, enable for internal teams, gather feedback, iterate
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Drift scorer may amplify noisy signals -> Mitigation: ensemble of metrics with tunable weights and minimum sample thresholds
Risk: Auto actions could cause disruption -> Mitigation: default to proposal-only mode; require explicit enable + two-person approval for production; provide dry-run mode
Risk: Telemetry volume increase -> Mitigation: sampling budget, incremental rollout, and backpressure on scorer ingest nodes
Risk: Trace linking may expose PII -> Mitigation: reuse existing redaction pipeline and require security review before GA
